name: Hera
summary: Queen of the Olympian gods, goddess of marriage, women, and family. Wife and sister of Zeus, known for her fierce protection of the sanctity of marriage and her relentless pursuit of Zeus's mortal lovers and their children.
cultural_context: Hera was one of the most important goddesses in Greek public religion, with major sanctuaries at Argos and Samos. Her worship emphasized marriage, queenship, fertility, and the protection of legitimate households and communities.
domain_role: Marriage, women, family, childbirth, queenship of the gods
origin_story: Hera was a daughter of the Titans Cronus and Rhea, and thus sister to Zeus, Poseidon, Hades, Demeter, and Hestia. After the Olympians' victory over the Titans, she became Zeus's wife and queen. Their courtship, in one version, began when Zeus transformed into a wounded cuckoo bird to win her sympathy.
achievements: Served as the presiding deity over marriage and married women across the Greek world
Maintained major cult centers at Argos and Samos, among the oldest and most important in Greece
A central figure in the Judgment of Paris, one of the mythic causes of the Trojan War
Supported the Greeks during the Trojan War, in opposition to Aphrodite and the Trojans
Protected the sanctity of marriage and the legitimacy of royal families through her worship
Supported Jason and the Argonauts during their dangerous search for the Golden Fleece

signature_quote.text: I am Hera, queen of the gods.
signature_quote.note: The title emphasizes Hera's authority over marriage, queenship, family, and the order of Olympus.
